title: Date a prepped food tub: peel a day label off the dispenser at its bar and press it flat onto the tub's lid
instruction: Put today's label on the lid of the food tub. Today is Wednesday.
context: Food preparation workers and cooks label every container of prepped food with the day it was made so stock is used first in, first out; health inspectors check for it. The labels come on rolls in a multi-roll dispenser, one colour per day. The right day's label stands a little way out past the dispenser's metal bar: it is pinched by that tab and drawn straight out, so it comes off its backing at the bar, then laid on the lid and pressed down all over with a fingertip. The label is thin and its back is sticky: pinched too shallow or pulled the wrong way it stays on the roll, laid crooked it hangs over the lid's edge, and a part not pressed down peels up in the walk-in and the date is lost. Taking a neighbouring roll's label by mistake wastes it and mislabels the food.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter (the table top). 1) Label dispenser: a DayMark IT111081 seven-slot plastic label dispenser for 2 in rolls, white, 445 wide (y) x 191 deep (x) x 114 tall, standing on the counter with its front face at x 290 and its centre line at y -72; it does not move (non-skid pads). Seven bays 58.7 wide between 3 mm dividers, centres 61.7 apart. Left to right as the robot faces it: Monday (blue, bay centre y 113), Tuesday (yellow, 51), Wednesday (red, -10), Thursday (brown, -72), Friday (green, -134), Saturday (orange, -195), Sunday (black, -257), in DayMark's day colours; a colour tab under each bay and, below it on the front face from 6 to 42 above the counter, the bay's day in black capitals 36 tall and 15 wide (MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN; each word 51 long), printed on a paper strip taped on for the trials. In each bay a roll of DayMark DissolveMark 2 x 2 in day labels (50.8 x 50.8, paper, about 0.1 thick, 250 to a roll; roll 60 across on a 27 core, estimate) sits on an axle 142 behind the front face; its strip runs forward over a flat deck to the metal dispenser bar along the front top edge, 100 above the counter (estimate), where the backing turns sharply down and back. Each roll's first label lies on the deck with its front 15 out past the bar's edge (x 275 to 326); the next label waits 3 behind it. Each label has a header in its day's colour printed with the day's full name in white capitals about 6 tall (WEDNESDAY on Wednesday's) and white write-on lines below it. 2) Tub: a Cambro 2SFSCW 2 qt CamSquare polycarbonate food container, 184 x 184 x 98, 257 g, with its SFC2 polyethylene snap lid on (190 square; its flat top 106 above the counter, estimate), centred at (165, -170), sides along x and y. For repeatable trials it holds no food: in place of prepped food it holds the same mass, 350 g, of plastic stuffing beads (Fairfield Poly-Fil Poly-Pellets), weighed on a kitchen scale and sealed in a quart freezer zip bag (177 x 188), laid flat and spread evenly over the tub's floor so it cannot shift; tub, lid (about 80 g, estimate) and beads about 687 g. Peel of a label from its backing about 0.1 N per 25 mm of width (estimate); the pressed label holds to the lid with about 1 N per quarter (estimate). Pressing a quarter down takes a fingertip press of at least 1 N: 9.8 kPa (100 gf/cm2), the contact pressure of the standard probe-tack test for pressure-sensitive adhesives (ASTM D2979), over about 1 cm2 of fingertip (estimate). Frictions (estimates): label on the backing 0.45, label on the lid 0.55, tub on the counter 0.4. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, hinge and mass.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run with a ruler, a photo and a feeler (a business card). The label is read as four quarters, 12.7 wide bands across its length. Stuck quarter: it lies flat on the lid's top (no corner more than 2 above it) and was pressed there with a fingertip (in simulation: a fingertip touching its top face, no stand-off, and pressing with at least 1 N; hovering over it or brushing it does not count); in a real trial, the card pushed against its edges does not slip under it and nothing lifts. Let go: both grippers' centre points at least 30 from the label. Scores: 1.0 for the Wednesday label off its roll, wholly on the lid's flat top (inside its 186 x 186 panel), let go, all four quarters stuck, held for 1 s. 0.5 + 0.125 per stuck quarter (0.5 to 0.875) for the same with fewer quarters stuck. 0.25 for the Wednesday label off its roll but not wholly on the lid's top (over its edge, on its side, on the counter, on the dispenser) or still held (a label stuck to the gripper counts as held). 0 for: any part of the Wednesday label still on its backing; the label folded onto its own adhesive (any fold past 150 degrees); any other day's label pulled more than 10 out of place or peeled up 1.5 from its backing at any time, even if put back; the tub tipped more than 20 degrees at any time or more than 30 from its mark at the end; (real trials) the dispenser moved more than 10 or a roll lifted out. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.625, 0.75, 0.875, 1.0.
reset_notes: Peel any label off the lid (DissolveMark labels also wash off) and throw away used labels. Draw each roll's strip until its first label stands 15 mm past the bar, on the bay's centre line; rewind or trim a label pulled further. Stand the tub on its mark, sides along x and y (the simulation shifts it by up to 10 mm in x and y each trial). The dispenser stays put.
fidelity: Each label is four rigid quarters on stiff hinges (bends, no crease), 0.8 mm thick and 5 g (real ~0.1 mm, ~0.3 g: lighter bodies are unstable). Adhesive is a force rule: a quarter on the backing is held by 0.4 N until drawn past the bar or peeled 1.5 mm up; one flat on the lid sticks (1 N, until peeled 2 mm up) only when a touching fingertip (gap <= 0.05 mm) presses it with >= 1 N; one press sticks a whole quarter. Never sticks to the pads. Backing and rolls are fixed. Forces are estimates.
